questions.question: Weight of A is 20% more than weight of B, whose weight is 30% more than weight of C. By how much percent weight of A is more than weight of C?
questions.questionHtml: Weight of A is 20% more than weight of B, whose weight is 30% more than weight of C. By how much percent weight of A is more than weight of C?
questions.solution:
Given:

Weight of A is 20% more than weight of B

weight of B is 30% more than weight of C.

Concept used:

Final Value = Actual Value + (Actual value × %age increase)

Calculation:

Let value of C be 100x

Value of B = 100x + [(100x × 30)/100] = 130x

Value of A = 130x + [(130x × 20)/100] = 156x

So,

The weight of A is (156x – 100x) = 56x more than C.

The weight of A is (56x × 100)/100 = 56% more than C

∴ The weight of A is 56% more than C

questions.question: By what percent the new price of the article must be increased to restore its former value, if the cost of the article is cut by 25% in the past?
questions.questionHtml: By what percent the new price of the article must be increased to restore its former value, if the cost of the article is cut by 25% in the past?
questions.solution:
Given:

An article price was reduced by 25%.
Formula used:

percentage increase = \(\frac{\text{new price}}{\text{old price}}\times 100 - 100 \)
Calculation:

Let the old price of the article be Rs.100, which reduced to Rs. 75.

percentage increase = \(\frac{100}{75}\times 100-100 =133.3 -100=33.3\)

∴ The present price of the article must be increased by\(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) to restore its former value.

questions.question: If the price of tea is increased by 40%, by how what percentage must the consumption of tea be decreased so as not to increase the expenditure?
questions.questionHtml: If the price of tea is increased by 40%, by how what percentage must the consumption of tea be decreased so as not to increase the expenditure?
questions.solution:
Let Original Consumption = 1 unit.

100 × 1 = 140 × New Consumption

⇒ New Consumption = 100/140 = 5/7

Decrease in Consumption = 1 - (5/7) = (2/7)

Percentage Decrease = (2/7) × 100  = \(28\frac{4}{7}\)%

questions.question: If the length and the breadth of a rectangle are increased by 15% and 20%, respectively, then by how much percent the area of the rectangle will increase?
questions.questionHtml: If the length and the breadth of a rectangle are increased by 15% and 20%, respectively, then by how much percent the area of the rectangle will increase?
questions.solution:
⇒ Length after increase of 15% = x + 15% of x = \(\frac{23x}{20}\)

⇒ Breadth after increase of 20% = y + 20% of y = \(=\frac{6y}{5}\)

⇒ New area of rectangle = \(\frac{23x}{20}× \frac{6y}{5}=\frac{69xy}{50}\)

⇒ Increase in area = \(\frac{69xy}{50}-xy=\frac{69xy-50xy}{50}=\frac{19xy}{50}\)

⇒ Percentage increase in the area of the rectangle = \(\frac{\frac{19xy}{50}}{xy}× 100=\frac{19}{50}× 100=38\%\)

here, the (-) sign shows decreased

questions.question: How much percentage should a racer increase speed to reduce the time by 20% to cover a fixed distance?
questions.questionHtml: How much percentage should a racer increase speed to reduce the time by 20% to cover a fixed distance?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Time reduces to 20% to cover a fixed distance 

FORMULA USED:

Distance = Speed × Time 

CALCULATION:

Here, according to the given question distance is fixed 

Now, let us assume the required time be t 

So, the reduces by 20% = t × 80/100 = 4t/5 

Distance = Speed × Time 

Original speed × t =  New speed × 4t/5  [As, distance is equal]

Original speed /New speed = 4t/5 ×1/t 

Original speed /New speed = 4/5 

Percentage increase in speed = 1/4 × 100 = 25% 

Hence, the percentage increase in speed is 25%.

questions.question: Nakul went to the market to buy groceries. He has some money with him, 20% of which he used to buy wheat flour, 25% of the remaining money is spent on cooking oils. If he is left with Rs. 900, then find out total amount of money that Nakul had.
questions.questionHtml: Nakul went to the market to buy groceries. He has some money with him, 20% of which he used to buy wheat flour, 25% of the remaining money is spent on cooking oils. If he is left with Rs. 900, then find out total amount of money that Nakul had.
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount of money left with Nakul after buying groceries = Rs. 900

Calculation:

Let the total amount of money that Nakul had be "M".

First, Nakul used 20% of his money to buy wheat flour. This means he spent (20/100)M on wheat flour, leaving him with (80/100)M.

Next, Nakul spent 25% of the remaining money on cooking oils. Therefore, the amount of money left after this expenditure is (75/100) × (80/100)M.

According to the given information, Nakul is left with Rs. 900, so we can set up the equation:

(75/100) × (80/100)M = 900

To find the total amount of money (M), divide both sides of the equation by [(75/100) × (80/100)]:

M = 900/[(75/100) × (80/100)]

Simplifying the equation:

M = 900/(75/100) × (100/80)

M = 900/(3/4) × (4/5)

M = 900 × (4/3) × (5/4)

M = 1500

Therefore, the total amount of money that Nakul had is Rs. 1500.

questions.question: The production of AB Co. increased by 10% after one year, and in the next year it increased by 22%. In the third year, it increased by 5%. What overall change (in %) has been there in the production in three years from the original production?
questions.questionHtml: The production of AB Co. increased by 10% after one year, and in the next year it increased by 22%. In the third year, it increased by 5%. What overall change (in %) has been there in the production in three years from the original production?
questions.solution:
Given:

Increase after one year = 10%

Increase in second year = 22%

Increase in third year = 5%

Calculation:

⇒ Let the production of the company be 100.

⇒ Production after one year = 100 + 10% of 100

⇒ Production after one year = 100 + \(\frac{10}{100}\times 100\) = 100 + 10 = 110

⇒ Production after second year = 110 + 22% of 110

⇒ Production after second year = 110 + \(\frac{22}{100}\times 110\) = 110 + 24.2 = 134.2

⇒ Production after third year = 134.2 + 5% of 134.2

⇒ Production after third year = 134.2 + \(\frac{5}{100}\times 134.2\) = 134.2 + 6.7 = 140.9

⇒ Change in the production = 140.9 – 100 = 40.9%

Therefore, the change in the production from last three years is 40.9%.

questions.question: The price of sugar is decreased by 10% By what percent can a person increase the consumption so that there is no change in the expenditure?
questions.questionHtml: The price of sugar is decreased by 10% By what percent can a person increase the consumption so that there is no change in the expenditure?
questions.solution:
Detailed solution∶

Let the price of the sugar be 100x

Price of sugar after decreased = 100x × (90/100) = 90x

Price ratio of sugar before and after = 100x ∶ 90x

As we know, consumption of sugar is inversely proportional to price

So, consumption ratio of sugar before and after decreasing = 90x ∶ 100x

Consumption increased by = 100x - 90x = 10x

Required percentage = (10x/90x) × 100 = (100/9) %

questions.question: In an examination, 45% of all the students who appeared are boys and the rest are girls. If 60% of the boys and 70% of the girls passed, then what is the percentage of students who failed?
questions.questionHtml: In an examination, 45% of all the students who appeared are boys and the rest are girls. If 60% of the boys and 70% of the girls passed, then what is the percentage of students who failed?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the total number of students in the examination be 100.

Number of boys = 45, which means number of girls = 55.

Boys who failed = (100 − 60)% of 45 = 40% of 45 = 18.

Girls who failed = (100 − 70)% of 55 = 30% of 55 = 16.5.

Total failed percentage = 18 + 16.5 = 34.5%.

∴ The correct answer is 34.5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total students considered = 100%

Percentage of boys = 45%

Passed boys = 60%

Passed girls = 70%

Formula Used:

Failed % = 100% − Passed %

Calculations:

⇒ Percentage of girls = 100% − 45% = 55%

⇒ Number of boys failed out of 100 = 40% of 45 = (40 ÷ 100) × 45 = 18

⇒ Number of girls failed out of 100 = 30% of 55 = (30 ÷ 100) × 55 = 16.5

⇒ Total failed students = 18 + 16.5 = 34.5

⇒ Percentage of students who failed = (34.5 ÷ 100) × 100% = 34.5%

∴ The correct answer is 34.5%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change

Percentage change is calculated as ((New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value) × 100.

Successive Percentage

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

Base Shift Rule

If A is R% more than B, then B is (R ÷ (100 + R)) × 100% less than A.

questions.question: In an office, 80% workers are men while 20% are women. The average age of the men is 30 and the average age of the women is 40. What is the average age of all the workers in that office?
questions.questionHtml: In an office, 80% workers are men while 20% are women. The average age of the men is 30 and the average age of the women is 40. What is the average age of all the workers in that office?
questions.solution:
Given:

80% of workers are men while 20% are women

The average age of the men is 30

The average age of the women is 40

Formula Used:

Average= \(\frac{Sum\space of\space Ages}{Total\space Worker}\)

Calculations:

Let the total number of workers be 100

⇒ Number of men's workers= 80% of total worker= 80 men

⇒ Number of women workers= 20% of total worker= 20 women

According to the formula,

⇒ Average= \(\frac{Sum\space of\space Ages}{Total\space Worker}\)

⇒ 30= \(\frac{Sum\space of\space Ages}{80}\)

⇒ Sum of ages of men= 30 x 80= 2400

similarly,

⇒ Average= \(\frac{Sum\space of\space Ages}{Total\space Worker}\)

⇒ 40= \(\frac{Sum\space of\space Ages}{20}\)

⇒ Sum of ages of women= 40 x 20= 800

Now, 

⇒ The average age of total workers =  \(\frac{Sum\space of\space Ages}{Total\space Worker}=\frac{2400+800}{100}=\frac{3200}{100}\)= 32

Hence, The average age of total worker is 32

questions.question: Out of two numbers, 20 percent of the smaller number is equal to 14 percent of the larger number. If the sum of both the numbers is 8942, then what is the value of the larger number?
questions.questionHtml: Out of two numbers, 20 percent of the smaller number is equal to 14 percent of the larger number. If the sum of both the numbers is 8942, then what is the value of the larger number?
questions.solution:
Given:

20% of x = 14% of y

Calculation:

Let the smaller number be x

Let the larger number be y

20/100 ×  x = 14/100 ×  y

⇒ x/y = 7/10

We know that the sum of both numbers is 8942.

Therefore, x + y = 8942

Substituting x/y = 7/10, we get:

x = (7/10) × y

Substituting this value of x in the equation x + y = 8942, we get:

(7/10) × y + y = 8942

⇒ (17/10) × y = 8942

⇒ y = 8942/(17/10)

⇒ y = 5260

Hence, the larger number is 5260.

∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 88% of the votes is elected by a majority of 684 votes. What is the total number of votes polled? (all polled votes are valid)
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 88% of the votes is elected by a majority of 684 votes. What is the total number of votes polled? (all polled votes are valid)
questions.solution:
Let total votes be V. Candidate A gets 88%, Candidate B gets 12%

 

Difference = 88% - 12% = 76%

 

Total votes = Majority votes / (Difference / 100)

 

V = 684 / (76 / 100)

 

V = (684 × 100) / 76

 

 

V = 900

questions.question: Tilak's salary increases by 15% in the first year, decreases by 20% in the second year and increases by 25% in the third year. If Tilak's salary after these three years is Rs. 23,000, then find the salary of Tilak in the beginning of these 3 years.
questions.questionHtml: Tilak's salary increases by 15% in the first year, decreases by 20% in the second year and increases by 25% in the third year. If Tilak's salary after these three years is Rs. 23,000, then find the salary of Tilak in the beginning of these 3 years.
questions.solution:
Concept Used:

New Value = Original Value × (1 ± Percentage/100)

Calculation:

For the third year, the salary increased by 25%, so the original salary before this increase was:

23,000 ÷ (1 + 25/100) = 23,000 ÷ 1.25 = Rs. 18,400

For the second year, the salary decreased by 20%, so the original salary before this decrease was:

18,400 ÷ (1 - 20/100) = 18,400 ÷ 0.8 = Rs. 23,000

For the first year, the salary increased by 15%, so the original salary before this increase was:

23,000 ÷ (1 + 15/100) = 23,000 ÷ 1.15 = Rs. 20,000 

So, Tilak's salary at the beginning of these three years was Rs. 20,000.

questions.question: Due to decrease in manpower, the production in a factory decreases by 25%. By what per cent should the working hours be increased to restore the original production?
questions.questionHtml: Due to decrease in manpower, the production in a factory decreases by 25%. By what per cent should the working hours be increased to restore the original production?
questions.solution:
Given:

Due to decrease in manpower, the production in a factory decreases by 25%.

We need to find by what percent the working hours should be increased to restore the original production.

Concept:

To restore the original production, the product of manpower and working hours should remain constant.

Formula Used:

Let the original working hours be H and the increased working hours be H'.

Let the original production be P and the decreased production be 0.75P (since it decreased by 25%).

To restore the original production:

P = 0.75P × (H'/H)

Calculation:

We have,

⇒ 1 = 0.75 × (H'/H)

⇒ H'/H = 1/0.75

⇒ H'/H = 4/3

⇒ H' = 4H/3

Percentage increase in working hours:

⇒ [(4H/3) - H]/H × 100%

⇒ (4H - 3H)/(3H) × 100%

⇒ H/(3H) × 100%

⇒ 1/3 × 100

⇒ 33 (1/3)%

∴ The correct answer is option 1.

questions.questionHtml: What will be a single equivalent discount for successive discounts of 20%, 40% and 75% on the marked price of an item?
questions.solution:
Given: 

The successive discount are 20%, 40% and 75%.

Formula:

Successive discount = X + Y \(-\frac{XY}{100}\)

Where,

X = First discount

Y = Second discount

Calculation:

Successive discount = \(X+Y-\frac{XY}{100}\)

\(20+40-\frac{(20×40)}{100}\) = 52%

Now, again

Successive discount = \(X+Y-\frac{XY}{100}\)

⇒ X = 52%, Y = 75%

⇒ \(52+75-\frac{(52×75)}{100}\)

⇒ \(127-39\)

⇒ \(88\)

∴ The single equivalent discount is 88%.

questions.question: The price of an electronic watch is first reduced by 25% and then increased by 50%. If the resulting price of the electronic watch is Rs. 7,650, then what was its original price (in Rs.)?

questions.question: Initial value of a car is Rs. 20000. The value of car depreciated by 20 percent of its initial value each year. What will be its value after 3 years?
questions.questionHtml: Initial value of a car is Rs. 20000. The value of car depreciated by 20 percent of its initial value each year. What will be its value after 3 years?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

A depreciation of 20% means the value becomes 80% or 4/5 of the previous year's value.

Value after 3 years = 20000 × (4/5)3

⇒ 20000 × (64/125)

⇒ 160 × 64 = 10240

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10240.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Value (P) = Rs. 20000

Rate of Depreciation (R) = 20%

Time Period (n) = 3 years

Formula Used:

Value after n years = P × (1 − R/100)n

Calculations:

⇒ Final Value = 20000 × (1 − 20/100)3

⇒ Final Value = 20000 × (80/100)3

⇒ Final Value = 20000 × (0.8)3

⇒ Final Value = 20000 × 0.512

⇒ Final Value = 10240

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10240.

Additional Information

Depreciation (Reducing Balance)

When value decreases by a fixed percentage on the current book value, use: V = P(1 − r/100)n.

Appreciation (Growth)

When the value of an asset or population increases over time, use: V = P(1 + r/100)n.

Straight Line Depreciation

If depreciation is a fixed amount calculated only on the initial cost: Total Depreciation = (Initial Value × Rate × Time) / 100.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of x% and y%, the net effective change is [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

questions.question: A number increased by 20% gives 240. Find the number.
questions.questionHtml: A number increased by 20% gives 240. Find the number.
questions.solution:
Given:

A number increased by 20% gives 240.

Formula Used:

The formula to calculate the original number when increased by a percentage is:

Original number = Increased number / (1 + Percentage increase)

Calculation:

Let the original number be x .

It is given that the number increased by 20% gives 240.

Hence,

x + 0.2x = 240

⇒ 1.2x = 240

⇒ x = 240 / 1.2

⇒ x = 200

The original number is 200.

questions.question: The number of persons raise by 20% to 30,942 in a year. What was the population originally a year ago?
questions.questionHtml: The number of persons raise by 20% to 30,942 in a year. What was the population originally a year ago?
questions.solution:
Given:

Increase in 1 year = 20%

Population after increase = 30,942

Calculation:

⇒ Let the population a year ago be x.

⇒ So, x + 20% of x = 30942

⇒ x + \(\frac{20}{100}\) × x = 30942

⇒ x + \(\frac{x}{5}\) = 30942

⇒ \(\frac{5x+x}{5}\) = 30942

⇒ x = \(\frac{30942\times 5}{6}\) = 5157 × 5 = 25785

Therefore, the population originally a year ago was 25785.

questions.question: In an institute, 35% are boys and the rest are girls. If 30% of the boys failed and 60% of the girls passed in an examination, then the percentage of the students who failed in the examination is:
questions.questionHtml: In an institute, 35% are boys and the rest are girls. If 30% of the boys failed and 60% of the girls passed in an examination, then the percentage of the students who failed in the examination is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The percentage of boys in an institute = 35%

Formula used:

\(GM\%\ =\ {GM\over TM}\ × 100\)     Where, GM = Gain marks, and TM = Total marks

Calculation:

Let the total number of students be X

According to the question

The number of boys = \({35X\over 100}\ =\ 0.35X\)

The number of girls = X - 0.35X = 0.65X

The number of boys who failed = 0.35X × \({30\over 100}\ =\ 0.105X\)

The number of girls who passed = 0.65X \(\times {60\over 100}\ =\ 0.39X\)

The number of girls who failed = 0.65X - 0.39X = 0.26X

The number of students who failed = 0.105X + 0.26X = 0.365X

The required percentage = \({0.365X\over X}\ \times 100\ =\ 36.5\%\)

∴ The required result will be 36.5%.

questions.question: A is 40% less than B, and C is 40% of the sum of A and B. The difference between A and B is what percentage of C?
questions.questionHtml: A is 40% less than B, and C is 40% of the sum of A and B. The difference between A and B is what percentage of C?
questions.solution:
Let the value of B be 100.

Value of A = 100 × (60/100) = 60

Value of C = (60 + 100) × (40/100) = 64

Required difference = [(100 – 60)/64] × 100 = 62.5%

questions.question: The ratio between the monthly income and the expenditure of Vaidic is 8 ∶ 5. If his income increases by 20% and his expenditure increases by 30%, then find the percentage increase or decrease in his monthly savings.
questions.questionHtml: The ratio between the monthly income and the expenditure of Vaidic is 8 ∶ 5. If his income increases by 20% and his expenditure increases by 30%, then find the percentage increase or decrease in his monthly savings.
questions.solution:
Let the monthly income and the expenditure of Vaidic be 8a and 5a respectively.

Income = 8a(1 + 20%) ⇒ I = 8a(1 + 0.20) ⇒ I = 9.6a

Expenditure = 5a(1 + 30%) ⇒ E = 5a(1 + 0.30) ⇒ E = 5a(1.30) = Rs. 6.5a

Savings = 9.6a - 6.5a = Rs. 3.1a

The total increase in savings  = [(3.1a - 3a/3a)] × 100⇒ S% = 10/3 ⇒ S = 3(1/3)%

questions.question: An alloy contains 32% copper 24% nickel and rest zinc. How much zinc is present in 12 kg of the alloy?
questions.questionHtml: An alloy contains 32% copper 24% nickel and rest zinc. How much zinc is present in 12 kg of the alloy?
questions.solution:
Given, the alloy contains 32% copper, 24% nickel and rest zinc, then

Percentage of zinc in the alloy = 100% - 32% - 24% = 44%

Quantity of zinc in 12 kg alloy = 12 × (44/100) = 5.28 kg.

questions.question: When a number is successively decreased by 25 percent, 40 percent and 20 percent, then it becomes 32,904. What is that number?
questions.questionHtml: When a number is successively decreased by 25 percent, 40 percent and 20 percent, then it becomes 32,904. What is that number?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Let the number be A.

According to question,

(100 - 25)/100 × (100 - 40)/100 × (100 - 20)/100 × A = 32904

75/100 × 60/100 × 80/100 × A = 32904

3/4 × 3/5 × 4/5 × A = 32904

9/25 × A = 32904

A = 32904 × 25/9

A = 3656 × 25

A = 91400

∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: After an increase of 9% in salary, a person received Rs. 6,300. What was his salary before the increase (consider integral part only)?
questions.questionHtml: After an increase of 9% in salary, a person received Rs. 6,300. What was his salary before the increase (consider integral part only)?
questions.solution:
Given:

After a 9% increase in salary, a person received Rs. 6,300.

Formula Used:

New Salary = Original Salary × (1 + Percentage Increase)

Calculation:

Let the original salary be x. After a 9% increase, the salary becomes:

New Salary = x × (1 + 0.09)

New Salary = x × 1.09

According to the question:

1.09 × x = 6300

⇒ x = 6300 / 1.09

⇒ x ≈ 5779

The salary before the increase was Rs. 5,779.
